1.explanation:
1) src/ol/layer/Heatmap.js declares and stores the className option on the Heatmap layer but does not actually force the renderer to use it.  
2) src/ol/renderer/canvas/Layer.js is where each canvas-based layer creates its wrapping <div> and <canvas> and currently hard-codes the CSS class to “ol-layer” (and skips setting any class on the <canvas>). Because the renderer never reads the layer’s className property, the user’s custom className option is ignored. These two files therefore need to be updated so that the renderer reads layer.getClassName() (falling back to the default) instead of using the literal “ol-layer” string.
1.bug_scenario: In the user’s sandbox they create a new Heatmap layer and pass in a custom className (e.g. “ol-layer-heatMap”) in the options, but when the map renders the layer’s DOM still uses the hard-coded “ol-layer” class on the layer container <div> (and no class at all on the <canvas>), so the user’s custom className never shows up in the page.

2.explanation: 1) src/ol/layer/Heatmap.js is the layer constructor where we accept `{className}` in the options but never actually declare a default class name (unlike other layer types) nor mark Heatmap as a standalone canvas‐renderer type.  2) src/ol/renderer/Map.js is where OL decides which container (and its classList) to create for each layer type. Heatmap currently falls into the generic “vector” bucket (sharing one canvas) and never picks up the layer’s own `className` or default class. Both files must be updated so that Heatmap layers get their own container (or at least have their reserved default class) and so that any passed‐in `className` is forwarded to the DOM.
2.bug_scenario: In the user’s codesandbox screenshot we see that passing a `className` option to a new `HeatmapLayer({ className: 'ol-layer-heatMap', … })` has no effect – the DOM still only shows the single shared vector‐canvas inside a `<div class="ol-layer">`, and neither the default nor the custom class name ever makes it onto the layer container or canvas. In other words, `className` is being dropped for Heatmap layers (and they never even get the default ‘ol-layer-heatmap’ class), so you cannot style them independently.
